note: Literature strongly supports the dichotomy between heterozygous loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency causing motor neuropathies and dominant-negative in-frame/missense variants causing epileptic encephalopathy.

evidence.text: Heterozygous nonsense mutations in SPTAN1 trigger nonsense-mediated decay and haploinsufficiency leading to juvenile-onset hereditary motor neuropathy, contrasting with dominant-negative mutations causal in epilepsy phenotypes.

source.title: Nonsense mutations in alpha-II spectrin in three families with juvenile onset hereditary motor neuropathy
source.quote: The mutant mRNA containing nonsense mutations is broken down by nonsense-mediated decay and leads to reduced protein levels in patient cells. Previously, dominant-negative αII-spectrin gene mutations were described as causal in a spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes.

numbers.metric: families with dominant hereditary motor neuropathy

evidence.text: Mutations in SPTAN1 lead to phenotypes spanning DEE5 to axonal neuropathy depending on dominant-negative versus haploinsufficiency pathogenic mechanisms.

source.title: Extending the clinical phenotype of SPTAN1: From DEE5 to migraine, epilepsy, and subependymal heterotopias without intellectual disability
source.quote: Mutations in SPTAN1 gene, encoding the nonerythrocyte αII-spectrin, are responsible for a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE5) and a wide spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders... A certain genotype–phenotype correlation has been proposed according to the type and location of the mutation.
